K=1 synthetic longitudinal recovery and estimability. The AML-shaped synthetic longitudinal
calibration experiment to assess the declared condition target contrasts disease with control.
Each symbol is one requested replicate positioned by mice per condition and expression feature
count; Shape identifies recovered and estimable, recovered but downstream non-estimable,
recovery below threshold, non-evaluable recovery, or execution failure outcomes. The analysis
unit is complete synthetic mouse trajectory; the estimand is axis recovery and downstream
estimability use separate declared denominators; time is recorded as collection time in weeks;
adjustment uses batch. Missing downstream rates indicate no recovered axis; recovered but
downstream interpretation was not estimable is retained separately from replicates that did not
recover the planted axis or lacked evaluable recovery evidence. Axis recovery uses one
canonical rule: loading cosine at least 0.9; its equivalent angle is descriptive. These
known-truth synthetic results describe recovery under the tested settings only; they do not
establish performance for biological data.
